draft.title: Ethical concepts in biology
card: honest, careful work. Researchers report results truthfully and do not make up, hide or change data.
fairness. The benefits and burdens of research are shared fairly, and no group is treated unfairly.
acting to do good. A study should aim to bring benefit, such as better health.
Non-maleficence is avoiding harm, so risks to people, animals or the environment are kept low. Respect is valuing the rights and choices of others, so people join freely after being told the facts.
draft.remember: Ask of any research: is it honest, fair, helpful, harmless and respectful?

a.q: A research team sets up a trial of a new drug. It tells each volunteer the possible risks and lets them choose freely whether to join. Which concept does this best show?
a.why: Telling people the facts and letting them choose freely shows respect for their rights and choices. Integrity is about honest reporting of results, which is not what the team is doing here.
a.clue: Think about who makes the choice to join.

b.q: A company tests a new vaccine and finds that some volunteers had a mild reaction. It leaves these results out of its report so the vaccine looks safer. Which concept is most clearly broken?
b.why: Leaving out results to change the picture is dishonest reporting, which breaks integrity. Beneficence is the tempting option, but the main fault is not about the aim of doing good. It is about being truthful with data.
b.clue: Focus on what was done with the results, not the vaccine itself.
